On 18 November 2026 at 10:16 UTC (11:16 CET), Voyager 1 becomes the first human-made object one light-day from Earth: about 26 billion km, the distance light travels in 24 hours. A command from Earth now takes a full day to reach it, and the reply another day to come back. It took 49 years, two months and 11 days to get there.

review.notes: Checked against NASA Science 'What Is a Light-Day' (modified 2026-11-12). Milestone 18 Nov 2026 5:16:07 a.m. EST = 10:16 UTC = 11:16 CET; chip and post match. Narration uses past tense ('is now', 'became'), so the post must go out after 10:16 UTC on 18 Nov (planned 17:00 UTC). A light-day is 25.9 billion km, rounded to 'about 26 billion'. Moon 1.3 s and Sun 8 min 20 s are NASA's own comparisons; the bars are drawn linearly to scale. The 24 h each way and the about-2-day round trip follow from the definition, and NASA says a signal takes 24 h to reach it. 49 y 2 mo 11 d and nearly 61,000 km/h match the page. 'Still sending data home' matches 'still returning data to us'. The images are real photos: the launch, the DSN antennas near Madrid (no claim that this station is the one talking to Voyager), and Pale Blue Dot.
